grammar.title: Present passive: is / are + past participle
grammar.explanation: Use is (for one thing) or are (for many things) with a past participle when the object or action is more important than who does it.
examples: This glass is made of ice.
Telescopes are used for looking at planets.
Many books are sold in that shop.

At the end, it is sent to the shop.
